solves.reasoning: (A) 'belief is so crucial in the placebo effect' — belief is essential (crucial), not trivial (unimportant). (B) Kaptchuk 'informs them about how powerful and effective placebos can be' — powerful (강력한), not feeble (약한). (C) '59 percent reported improvements' (positive outcomes), not setbacks (악화). → crucial-powerful-improvements = choice 2.

(A) 'deception is necessary' — the passage explicitly says deception is needed (seemingly), so deception (속임) fits. Sincerity contradicts this. (B) 'it could damage their trust' — discovering the placebo damages (해치다) trust. Strengthen is the opposite. (C) 'leading to doubt about future treatments' — doubt (의심) results. Confidence is the opposite. → deception-damage-doubt = choice 1.

(A) 'deception is necessary in order to trigger a patient's trust' — trigger means to cause/initiate trust. Suppress means to prevent, which is opposite. (B) 'results may seem modest' — the 59% vs 35% difference is not overwhelming, hence modest (겸손한/상당하지 않은). Remarkable would mean exceptional. (C) 'giving a placebo isn't the same as doing nothing' — the key point is placebos are NOT doing nothing. → trigger-modest-nothing = choice 3.

③ 'deterioration' is wrong. '59 percent of those on an open placebo treatment reported deterioration' — the passage says 59% reported improvements (positive outcomes). Deterioration means getting worse, which contradicts the positive trial result being used to show placebos work.

② 'secretly' is wrong. 'He tells patients secretly that they will be taking a placebo' — Kaptchuk's whole research point is to investigate placebos WITHOUT deception. He tells patients 'up front' (openly/frankly), not secretly. Secretly would mean he's still deceiving them.

④ 'something' is wrong. 'giving a placebo isn't the same as doing something' — the point of the passage is that giving a placebo IS doing something (it has real effects). The passage says 'isn't the same as doing nothing' — meaning a placebo IS something. 'Something' makes the sentence contradict the intended meaning.

Blank: 'informs them about how _____ and effective placebos can be.' The researcher is promoting placebo confidence, showing they work well. → 'powerful' (choice 2). Harmful/useless/ordinary would not be what a researcher uses to encourage placebo trust.

Blank: 'deception is necessary in order to _____ a patient's trust.' The purpose is to initiate/activate patient trust in the drug. → 'trigger' (choice 3). Eliminate/suppress would destroy trust; ignore is irrelevant.

Blank: 'is _____ the possibility of doing away with the element of deception.' Kaptchuk is actively researching/studying this possibility. → 'investigating' (choice 4). Abandoning/dismissing would mean he's not pursuing it; confirming implies he's already proven it.

'crucial' means extremely important or essential. Context: 'belief is so crucial in the placebo effect' = absolutely necessary. 'essential' (choice 1) is the closest synonym. Minor/optional are antonyms; temporary is unrelated to importance.

'modest' means not very large or impressive. Context: 'results may seem modest' = results are not spectacular. 'moderate' (choice 3) = of medium amount = closest synonym. Impressive/outstanding/significant are near-antonyms (all mean large/notable).

'deception' means the act of deceiving or misleading. Context: 'deception is necessary to trigger patient's trust' = tricking/misleading them. 'trickery' (choice 4) = deceitful acts = closest synonym. Honesty/clarity/sincerity are all antonyms.

'up front' means openly, directly, without concealing. Its antonym should mean secretly or in a hidden manner. 'covertly' (choice 3) = in a hidden/secretive way = direct antonym. Openly/directly/candidly are all synonyms of 'up front'.

'necessary' means required/essential. Its antonym should mean not required/optional. 'dispensable' (choice 4) = able to be dispensed with/not essential = direct antonym. Required/vital/essential are all synonyms of necessary.

(A) 'In one trial with irritable bowel syndrome' — 'trial' here = a clinical experiment/test = 임상 실험. (B) 'The trial of the accused lasted for three weeks' — 'trial' here = a legal proceeding in court = 재판. → (A) 임상 실험 - (B) 재판 = choice 2.

Definition: 'a substance with no therapeutic effect, used as a control in testing new drugs.' This exactly describes a placebo — an inert substance given to a control group. 'placebo' (choice 1). Deception/treatment/syndrome don't match this medical definition.
Blank: 'Because _____ (believe) is so crucial...' After 'Because', a noun subject is needed. 'believe' (verb) → noun form = 'belief' (믿음).
Blank: 'deception is _____ (necessity) in order to...' After linking verb 'is', an adjective predicate is needed. 'necessity' (noun) → adjective form = 'necessary'.

Blank: 'as compared with 35 percent of the _____ that received no treatment.' In clinical trials, there's a placebo group and a control group. Those who received NO treatment = the control group (대조군). → 'control group' (choice 1).

Blank: 'investigating the possibility of _____ the element of deception.' Kaptchuk's research goal is to eliminate/remove deception from placebo treatment. → 'doing away with' (choice 4) = removing/eliminating. Reinforcing/preserving/relying on all mean the opposite: keeping deception.
